fq_items.question: What exactly happens during a professional termite inspection visit?
fq_items.answer: Our technician will conduct a thorough visual examination of your home's interior and exterior, including the foundation, crawl spaces, attic, and any wood structures. We look for active colonies, mud tubes, damaged wood, and other signs of infestation. We'll use a moisture meter and sometimes a thermal imaging tool to identify high-risk areas. You'll receive a detailed report documenting findings and recommendations, whether treatment is needed or preventive measures are advised.

fq_items.question: How long does a termite inspection take and how many visits needed?
fq_items.answer: Most inspections take one to two hours, depending on your home's size and accessibility of key areas. In most cases, one visit is sufficient to assess the property thoroughly. If we detect an active infestation, we may recommend a follow-up visit to monitor treatment progress or confirm that the problem has been resolved. We'll explain the timeline clearly before starting.

fq_items.question: What time of year should I get a termite inspection in Littleton, CO?
fq_items.answer: Spring and early summer are peak activity seasons in Colorado's Front Range, when termites are most visible and colonies expand. However, infestations can occur year-round indoors. We recommend scheduling an inspection in spring as a preventive check, or immediately if you notice warning signs. Fall is also a good time before winter, when damage may go unnoticed.

fq_items.question: What are the warning signs my Littleton home needs termite treatment?
fq_items.answer: Common red flags include mud tubes along foundation walls or interior framing, hollow-sounding wood, buckling paint or wallpaper, and small holes in wood trim or flooring. You may also notice discarded wings near windowsills or light fixtures. Sagging floors or ceilings can indicate advanced damage. Don't wait—if you spot any of these signs, contact us for a prompt evaluation.

fq_items.question: How much does a termite inspection cost and do you offer free estimates?
fq_items.answer: We provide transparent pricing and offer free estimates for most residential inspections. Our team will discuss costs upfront before any work begins. Factors affecting pricing include your home's size, accessibility, and whether additional diagnostic tools are needed. Contact us for a no-obligation quote tailored to your property.

fq_items.question: Why hire a professional instead of trying DIY termite detection methods?
fq_items.answer: Professionals have the training, equipment, and experience to spot infestations that homeowners easily miss. Many DIY products address only surface-level problems and miss hidden colonies deep in walls or soil. Our systematic approach identifies the full scope of damage and the source, allowing us to eliminate the problem effectively rather than temporarily mask symptoms.

fq_items.question: How should I prepare my home before a termite inspection appointment?
fq_items.answer: Ensure clear access to your foundation, crawl space, attic, and basement by moving stored items away from walls. Make note of any areas where you've seen suspicious signs. Unlocking exterior gates or shed doors helps us inspect all vulnerable areas. You don't need to clean extensively—we're trained to work around normal household items. Let us know if any rooms are off-limits beforehand.

fq_items.question: What happens if termites return after treatment—is it guaranteed?
fq_items.answer: We stand behind our work with a warranty on completed treatments. If activity recurs within the coverage period, we'll return to address it at no additional charge. The length and terms of our guarantee depend on the treatment type and your home's conditions. We'll provide full details in writing so you understand what's covered and for how long.
